payload.detail: UPDATE 2026-09-26 (owner decisions relayed via the coordinator, 'yes to all five'; offline, no provider access; PR #3067): Mental Health Advocacy Service registered (catalogue identity only, code MHASWA). With the new last-updated date model, WA-MHAS and WA-MHERL are admitted as unverified ledger candidates on their own update stamps. WA-AHLO stays held (host not governed, version unknown); 4AT stays held (no agency, no date). PRIOR DETAIL: UPDATE 2026-09-26 (owner-approved page reads from the cloud session, no provider access): All four pages read. WA-AHLO is published by the Fiona Stanley Fremantle Hospitals Group (registered, code FSFHG) and states 'Last Updated: 20/02/2026'; WA-MHERL by the Mental Health Commission (registered, MHCWA), 'Page last updated 1 May 2025'; WA-MHAS by the Mental Health Advocacy Service (NOT in the authority register), 'Last updated: 7 November 2025'; 4AT's site names no agency ('© 2026 the4AT', credited to Prof Alasdair MacLullich, University of Edinburgh) and shows no date or version. Publisher fields corrected in dictionary-source-candidates.json and findings recorded in dictionary-source-dispositions.json. All four stay held: three give only a last-updated stamp (the register has no update event, same rule as the AIHW pages), MHAS needs an owner decision to register it (a retrieval-ranking surface), and 4AT needs a dated document. The registry comment contradiction (Government of Western Australia registered vs 'deliberately not registered') is unchanged because the registry was not edited. NEXT: owner decisions on the update-stamp event and on registering the Mental Health Advocacy Service. PRIOR DETAIL: WA-MHAS records 'Government of Western Australia', WA-AHLO records 'WA Health service providers', WA-MHERL records 'Mental Health Commission / WA Health' (two publishers in one field), and 4AT-OFFICIAL records '4AT developers'. None was registered in src/lib/source-authority-registry.ts on purpose: a catch-all entry for the Crown would resolve every WA government document to a single authority, which is worse than leaving the records held. Establish the actual publishing agency for each and correct the publisher field, then re-run npm run check:source-acquisitions. PARKED 2026-09-18 on the research, with two findings recorded that did not need it. The four canonical pages cannot be read from this environment: the network egress proxy answers 403 to CONNECT for wa.gov.au, fsfhg.health.wa.gov.au, mhc.wa.gov.au and the4at.com, verified directly by curl, so no publisher was established and all four stay held. WHAT WAS FOUND WITHOUT THE PAGES, now an open assurance decision (DICTIONARY-PUBLISHER-AGENCIES in docs/clinical-hazard-controls.json, visible in the developer hub): (1) source-authority-registry.ts:509 registers 'Government of Western Australia' as catalogue-identity-only, added 2026-09-16 by commit 255b9c1fe, while the comment at 558-564 still states that exact string was deliberately not registered - one of the two is wrong and the comment misleads the next reader; (2) correcting any publisher only clears the acquisition gate if the new name resolves in that register, which is a protected retrieval-ranking surface, so a metadata correction is also a retrieval change. Note tests/dictionary-sense-drafts.test.ts requires at least three of the four to keep the blocker, so at most one could ever be cleared alone. TO UNBLOCK: read the four page footers from an unrestricted network, or have the owner paste them.
